barker_yields.speaker: narrator
barker_yields.text: The Barker folded down onto the sawdust a joint at a time, the way a puppet does when the strings are let go. He was still talking.

barker_yields.speaker: barker
barker_yields.text: ...a passing shower, ladies and gentlemen, nothing more, do not be alarmed, keep your seats, the finale is about to—

barker_yields.speaker: patch
barker_yields.text: It wasn't a shower. You watched the water come in under the canvas. You told them to stay, because if they left the night was over, and then you were just a man with a megaphone, standing in the rain.

barker_yields.speaker: barker
barker_yields.text: ...They were having such a wonderful time.

barker_yields.speaker: patch
barker_yields.text: I know. I tell stories too. I told one about my tail to anyone who'd listen. It's easier than saying what happened. It's so much easier.

barker_yields.speaker: patch
barker_yields.text: Say it. Just once. Not to them. To me.

barker_yields.speaker: narrator
barker_yields.text: He said it quietly, without the megaphone. Then he reached up into the dark over the ring and pulled a cord, and all over Gatefold Fair, one string at a time, the lights went out.

barker_yields.speaker: narrator
barker_yields.text: The rain sounded different after that. It sounded like rain. Like something that could stop.
